    changes ~54 inline handlers, and unlike S2a a mistake there is
    behavioural rather than structural — it'd send a keystroke to the
    wrong view. With one view mounted, no test can catch that, because
    both answers are the same view. So S2b's real verification only
    arrives with S3.

  feedback from Architect 1:
        feat(web): a tap focuses its view, which is how a control
        finds it…)
    ⎿  43f51e4 feat(web): a tap focuses its view, which is how a
       control finds it
    ⎿  Allowed by auto mode classifier

  ⏺ S2b shipped (43f51e4). 118 node + 19 browser tests green.

    I did not build what the plan said. The plan was to thread this
    through 54 handlers and ~40 signatures. What shipped is one
    capture-phase listener on #terminalView, ~40 lines.

    The reason isn't line count. Spec §8 already says "clicking
    anywhere in a view focuses it" — focus and targeting are the same
    fact, and the capture phase runs before the target's own onclick,
    so every handler reading fv() is already reading its own view. The
    plan had built a second targeting mechanism alongside the focus
    model it had scheduled for S3, where it even noted the listener
    would land first and "that handler already targets its own view
    anyway." Two mechanisms, one job.

    The decisive argument is the one I flagged at the end of last
    turn: with one view mounted, a this threaded wrongly resolves to
    the same view as a correct one. 54 silent chances to send a
    keystroke to the wrong pane, no test able to tell. The listener is
    one mechanism and it's testable now — mount a second view, drive
    it. I verified each new assertion fails with the listener
    disabled, and the ruler regression fails against the old line.

    Three real bugs fixed along the way, all of which would have
    reached S3:

    - The ruler's pointerdown read e.target.id to pick the grabbed
    handle. S2a made those data-role, so it never matched — every
    press started a fresh one-line range instead of dragging an end. A
    selection you could make but not adjust, live on the branch right
    now.
    - armFire's 1.5s expiry and pressCtrl's 3s confirm re-read fv()
    when they fired. Two views means a live one-tap QUIT, CLS or
    Ctrl-D left armed on a view you walked away from — the exact
    accident the arm exists to prevent.
    - Nine listeners were bound to view 0's elements at load. A second
    view would have had no ruler, no composer keydown, no scroll.

    The S1 accessors stay, against the plan. fv() is now wrong in
    exactly one place — the poll/render path, where there's no user to
    have focused anything. Deleting them in S2b meant ~86 edits with


• Review S2b: capture focus routing, timer safety, ruler roles, per-view listeners, retained accessors.
